name: Government of the U.S. Virgin Islands

summary.text: The Government of the U.S. Virgin Islands, the territory where Jeffrey Epstein owned a private island, sued JPMorgan Chase in federal court in Manhattan, alleging the bank was indispensable to the operation and concealment of Epstein's trafficking enterprise and seeking at least $190 million. On 26 September 2023, weeks before trial, JPMorgan agreed to pay $75 million without admitting wrongdoing; the territory's Department of Justice said part of the sum would fund mental-health services for Epstein's survivors.

facts.claim: The U.S. Virgin Islands' suit argued that JPMorgan was 'indispensable to the operation and concealment of the Epstein trafficking enterprise' and that the bank did not raise red flags to law enforcement or regulators about Epstein as a high-risk customer making repeated large cash withdrawals; it sought penalties and disgorgement of at least $190 million.
facts.quote: indispensable to the operation and concealment of the Epstein trafficking enterprise

sources.title: JPMorgan to pay $75 million on claims that it enabled Jeffrey Epstein's sex trafficking operations
JPMorgan pays $75M to settle US Virgin Islands suit over Epstein ties

facts.claim: On 26 September 2023 JPMorgan Chase agreed to pay $75 million to the U.S. Virgin Islands to settle the claims, averting a trial set to start the following month; the bank did not admit wrongdoing.
facts.quote: JPMorgan Chase agreed Tuesday to pay US$75 million to the U.S. Virgin Islands to settle claims that the bank enabled the sex-trafficking acts committed by financier Jeffrey Epstein.

sources.title: JPMorgan to pay $75 million on claims that it enabled Jeffrey Epstein's sex trafficking operations
JPMorgan settles Epstein sex trafficking lawsuit with US Virgin Islands, to pay $75 million

facts.claim: JPMorgan said $55 million of the settlement would go to local charities assisting victims of domestic abuse and trafficking and to local law enforcement; the Virgin Islands Department of Justice said $10 million would create a fund for mental-health services for Epstein's survivors.
facts.quote: US$10 million will be used to create a fund to provide mental health services for Epstein's survivors

facts.claim: Bloomberg reported a different breakdown: $30 million for Virgin Islands anti-trafficking charities and a survivors' mental-health fund, $25 million for local infrastructure and law enforcement to prevent sex crimes, and $20 million in attorneys' fees.

sources.title: JPMorgan pays $75M to settle US Virgin Islands suit over Epstein ties

facts.claim: The settlement announcement also covered a separate, confidential settlement between JPMorgan and former executive Jes Staley, who had managed the Epstein relationship; JPMorgan had earlier agreed in June 2023 to pay $290 million to settle a class action by Epstein's victims.
facts.quote: the bank also reached a confidential legal settlement with James "Jes" Staley

openQuestions: Site claim tested: 'JPMorgan paid $290 million to Epstein's victims and $75 million to the Virgin Islands in 2023' — supported.
The Virgin Islands Department of Justice's own press release was not located; the fund breakdown differs between AP and Bloomberg accounts.
The territory's separate settlement with Epstein's estate (2022) was not researched here; the amount is not recorded.
